assigned:
Create one high-fidelity mobile-first product UI mockup as a flat portrait screenshot, 390 x 844, for the Turkish PWA Ev Hesap. It is the authenticated household dashboard for housemates who record shared expenses, see net balances, and manually settle only open expenses. This must read as a working app screen, not an illustration, marketing poster, or photograph. Keep all major Turkish UI copy exactly as specified below, with crisp legible letters and no filler text. Do not invent claims or dates.

Visual world: a contemporary apartment electrical distribution panel translated into a real shared-expense interface, not a literal photograph or sci-fi control deck. Flat geometry, screen-printed labels, porcelain-enamel light surface #EEF0EA, graphite ink #172124, steel-gray rules #5D6968, signal orange #E45A32, sparse amber state #D4AE43. Humanist sans for words; tabular monospaced numerals only for money and household code. No texture, grain, gradients, glow, perspective, photo, or faux metal.

Layout: a slim top strip with EV HESAP, household name Örnek Ev, and code EV-4K6P2R9D. A prominent page heading Açık hesap and sublabel Açık dönem · 3 harcama. Show the supporting amount ₺1.800 beside Açık gider toplamı, medium sized, not as a giant hero metric. Show three crisp member balance rows: Ece +₺500 alacaklı; Mert −₺100 borçlu; Deniz −₺400 borçlu. Use only a few thin straight conductor traces to connect the names to shared expenses; names and amounts remain more prominent than lines. Place an obvious primary action Harcama ekle and a quieter link Borçları hesapla. Below, an Açık harcamalar list with three rows: Pazar alışverişi · Ece ödedi · ₺900 · 3 kişi; Su faturası · Mert ödedi · ₺600 · 2 kişi; Temizlik malzemesi · Deniz ödedi · ₺300 · 3 kişi. The amounts total ₺1.800 and the balances are mathematically consistent with equal participant shares. Dense but breathable vertical hierarchy, true phone composition. No generic dashboard cards, rounded rectangles, shadows, floating icon tiles, decorative grids, or repeated metric tiles. The relationships and amounts must be the first thing a viewer understands.
